3-5.title: Our Favorite Recess Games
3-5.context: Room 12 voted for their favorite recess game. Each student voted one time.

questions.q: How many votes did Jump Rope get?
questions.why: The Jump Rope bar stops at 5, so Jump Rope got 5 votes.

questions.q: How many more votes did Tag get than Soccer?
questions.why: Tag got 12 votes and Soccer got 8 votes. 12 minus 8 is 4.

questions.q: Which sentence is true?

options.text: Jump Rope got the most votes.
Soccer got more votes than Four Square.
Four Square got more votes than Soccer.

questions.why: Four Square got 9 votes and Soccer got 8 votes, so Four Square got 1 more vote.

write.prompt: Write one sentence that compares two games. Use a number.
write.model: Tag got 12 votes, which is 4 more than Soccer.

3-5.title: How Our Bean Plant Grew
3-5.titleEs: Cómo creció nuestra planta de frijol
3-5.context: Our class planted a bean seed. We measured the plant's height at the end of each week.

questions.q: How tall was the plant in Week 3?
questions.why: The point for Week 3 is at 9, so the plant was 9 centimeters tall.

questions.q: How many centimeters did the plant grow from Week 1 to Week 4?
questions.why: The plant was 2 centimeters in Week 1 and 14 centimeters in Week 4. 14 minus 2 is 12.

questions.q: What happened to the plant's height over the four weeks?
questions.why: The line goes up every week: 2, 5, 9, then 14 centimeters.

write.prompt: Write one sentence about how the plant changed. Use a number from the chart.
write.model: The plant increased from 2 centimeters in Week 1 to 14 centimeters in Week 4.

3-5.title: How We Get to School
3-5.context: Students in one fourth grade class told how they get to school each morning.
frames: The most ___ get to school by ___.
The fewest ___ get to school by ___.

questions.q: How many students walk to school?
questions.why: The Walk bar stops at 10, so 10 students walk.

questions.q: How many more students ride the bus than come by car?
questions.why: 18 students ride the bus and 14 come by car. 18 minus 14 is 4.

questions.q: Which two groups together are equal to the Bus group?
questions.why: Car has 14 and Bike has 4. 14 plus 4 is 18, the same as Bus.

write.prompt: Write one sentence that compares two ways to get to school. Use a number.
write.model: Bus has the most students, 18, which is 8 more than Walk.

3-5.title: Animals in the Schoolyard
3-5.titleEs: Animales en el patio de la escuela
3-5.context: Our class went outside for one hour and counted the animals we saw in the schoolyard.
frames: We saw the same number of ___ and ___.

questions.q: How many birds did the class see?
questions.why: The Birds bar stops at 14, so the class saw 14 birds.

questions.q: Which two animals had the same number?
questions.why: Squirrels and Butterflies both have bars at 7, so the numbers are equal.

questions.q: Which sentence is true about the data?

options.text: The class saw fewer birds than rabbits.
The class saw more rabbits than squirrels.
The class saw twice as many birds as squirrels.

questions.why: There were 14 birds and 7 squirrels. 7 plus 7 is 14, so there were twice as many birds.

write.prompt: Write one sentence that compares two animals. Use a number.
write.model: We saw 14 birds, which is 7 more than squirrels.

6-8.title: Temperature Over One Day
6-8.context: A student recorded the outdoor temperature every three hours on a spring day, in degrees Fahrenheit.

chart.title: Outdoor temperature on a spring day

frames: The temperature rose from ___ ___ at ___ to ___ ___ at ___.

questions.q: What was the temperature at noon?
questions.why: The point for Noon is at 66, so it was 66 degrees.

questions.q: How many degrees did the temperature rise from 6 AM to 3 PM?
questions.why: It was 48 degrees at 6 AM and 70 degrees at 3 PM. 70 minus 48 is 22.

questions.q: Which sentence best describes the trend?

options.text: The temperature rose until 3 PM, then fell.
The temperature stayed the same all day.

questions.why: The line goes up from 48 to 70 degrees by 3 PM, peaks, then goes down to 61 degrees at 6 PM.

write.prompt: Write one sentence that describes how the temperature changed. Use a number and the unit.
write.model: The temperature peaked at 70 degrees at 3 PM, then fell 9 degrees by 6 PM.

6-8.title: A Growing Town
6-8.context: The town of Riverton counts its people every ten years. The chart shows the population from 1980 to 2020.
frames: From ___ to ___, the population increased from ___ to ___ ___.
From ___ to ___, the population stayed the same at ___ ___.

questions.q: What was the population of Riverton in 2000?
questions.why: The point for 2000 is at 4,500, so 4,500 people lived in Riverton.

questions.q: What happened to the population from 1980 to 1990?
questions.why: It went from 1,500 to 3,000 people. 1,500 times 2 is 3,000, so it doubled.

questions.q: Which sentence describes the population from 2010 to 2020?

options.text: It stayed the same at 6,000 people.

questions.why: The population was 6,000 in 2010 and 6,000 in 2020, so the line is flat.

write.prompt: Write one sentence about how the population of Riverton changed. Use numbers from the chart.
write.model: The population doubled from 1,500 people in 1980 to 3,000 people in 1990.

6-8.title: Does Recycling Make a Difference?
6-8.context: A middle school weighed the plastic it recycled each week. At the start of Week 2, the school put a recycling bin in every classroom.
frames: Plastic recycled rose from ___ ___ in ___ to ___ ___ in ___.

questions.q: How many pounds of plastic did the school recycle in Week 4?
questions.why: The point for Week 4 is at 45, so the school recycled 45 pounds.

questions.q: How many more pounds were recycled in Week 5 than in Week 1?
questions.why: The school recycled 48 pounds in Week 5 and 24 pounds in Week 1. 48 minus 24 is 24.

questions.q: Which claim is best supported by the data?

options.text: The classroom bins helped the school recycle more plastic.
The classroom bins made the school recycle less plastic.
The amount of plastic recycled stayed the same.

questions.why: After the bins arrived in Week 2, the amount rose every week, from 24 pounds to 48 pounds.

write.prompt: Write one sentence that makes a claim about the classroom bins. Support it with numbers from the chart.
write.model: The bins helped because recycling doubled from 24 pounds to 48 pounds.

6-8.title: The Book Fair Fundraiser
6-8.titleEs: La recaudación de fondos de la feria del libro
6-8.context: Three grades sold books at a school book fair to raise money for new library books.

questions.q: How much money did Grade 7 raise?
questions.why: The Grade 7 bar stops at 180, so Grade 7 raised 180 dollars.

questions.q: How many more dollars did Grade 8 raise than Grade 7?
questions.why: Grade 8 raised 300 dollars and Grade 7 raised 180 dollars. 300 minus 180 is 120.

questions.q: How much money did the three grades raise together?
questions.why: 240 plus 180 plus 300 is 720, so the grades raised 720 dollars together.

write.prompt: Write one sentence that compares the money raised by two grades. Use a number and the unit.
write.model: Grade 8 raised 300 dollars, which is 60 more than Grade 6.
